sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the nightshades work (2026-10-17): every character from the floras in the nightshades notes (plantgen-claude project-files/nightshades/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Circaea lutetiana, plant_name_id 2721837 (Library 1.0 list, read 2026-10-17).

growth_form.note: Its habit as the floras describe it, drawn by the forb form.

growth.note: Grown to the age it is drawn at: an annual's one season, a perennial's or shrub's few years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

generator.params.note: Drawing values no character gives (nightshades, 2026-10-17): a patch of stems from creeping rootstocks (Bentham p. 154) by eye from photographs (iNaturalist 176260134); thin stems; five leaf pairs below a raceme a third of the stem, about 14 flowers, by eye from photographs (iNaturalist 99562952).

traits.life_span.note: Bentham and Hooker, Handbook of the British Flora (1908 printing), Circaea lutetiana, p. 154 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): perennial by creeping rootstocks, the flowering stems annual.

traits.perennation.note: Wikipedia, 'Circaea lutetiana' (read 2026-10-17): the parts above ground die in winter, leaving a rhizome.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Circaea lutetiana' (read 2026-10-17): 20-60 cm, rarely 75 cm; Hooker p. 159: 1-2 ft.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Bentham and Hooker, Handbook of the British Flora (1908 printing), Circaea lutetiana, p. 154 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): broadly ovate or heart-shaped; Hooker: base rounded, truncate or cordate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Bentham and Hooker, Handbook of the British Flora (1908 printing), Circaea lutetiana, p. 154 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): rather coarsely toothed; Hooker and Wikipedia: faintly or weakly toothed.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Wikipedia, 'Circaea lutetiana' (read 2026-10-17): narrowing gradually to a pointed tip.

traits.leaf_base_shape.note: Wikipedia, 'Circaea lutetiana' (read 2026-10-17): base rounded or slightly notched; Hooker: rounded, truncate or cordate.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Bentham and Hooker, Handbook of the British Flora (1908 printing), Circaea lutetiana, p. 154 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 2-3 in; Hooker: 1-3 in.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Circaea lutetiana, p. 159 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): the petiole almost as long as the blade. Our reading of 'almost as long' against a 1-3 in blade.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Circaea lutetiana (now C. canadensis), p. 611 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers about 1.5 lines broad (3 mm), the North American plant's, as Hooker's own figure is unreadable.

traits.flower_colour.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Circaea lutetiana, p. 159 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers white or pink. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.fruit_type.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Circaea lutetiana, p. 159 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): fruit broadly obovoid, does not split open, each cell with one seed, covered with hooked bristles.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Circaea lutetiana' (read 2026-10-17): a small burr 3.5-5 mm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: ripe burr brown.

traits.fruit_posture.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Circaea lutetiana, p. 159 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): pedicels spreading in flower, reflexed in fruit; Bentham: turning down after flowering.

traits.flowering_months.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Circaea lutetiana, p. 159 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): June-August.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: fruit July-September.
